History:
- Presenting complaint: Right knee pain with clicking noted during running and gym activity; intermittent tingling in right toes (one episode).
- Onset/duration: Symptoms started approximately 2 weeks ago; increased running distance began about 1 month ago (training for a marathon).
- Progression/context: Pain typically begins ~20 minutes into runs (~2.5–3 miles), sometimes forces stopping runs; clicking noted with flexion/extension during gym abdominal exercises; initial mild swelling after first longer run resolved with ice; currently pain not present at rest.
- Associated features: One episode of right toe tingling after a run; no ongoing numbness, no calf pain, no color/temperature change in lower leg; able to fully straighten and fully flex the leg; no locking, no instability described.
- Provoking/relieving factors: Provoked by longer runs and certain gym movements; relieved with ice.
- Relevant prior events: Fall playing ice hockey a few months ago with a large bruise to unspecified area.

Past Medical History:
- Medical: No chronic illnesses reported. Past LASIK surgery for far-sightedness. Prior severe UTI that required ER evaluation (possible kidney stones considered).
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications (from patient report):
  - Ibuprofen — patient reports use, "400 mg max" (dose recorded by patient); route/frequency not documented.
  - Aleve — patient takes occasionally; dose/route/frequency not documented. (Patient uncertain about drug class.)
  - Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Xanax (occasional use) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Recreational cannabis: "smokes a joint" occasionally.
- Immunizations / other: Not documented.
- Social: Training for marathon; plays sports (ice hockey). No other substance use documented beyond cannabis; employment/living situation not clinically relevant beyond address confirmation.

Physical Examination:
- No formal clinician-performed exam documented (assessment performed via video history).
- Patient-reported/observed findings:
  - Mild swelling after initial long run which resolved with ice; currently no visible swelling.
  - Clicking with knee flexion/extension during gym activities.
  - Pain localized centrally with slight tendency to the right side of the right knee.
  - Full active range of motion reported (able to fully straighten and fully flex).
  - No locking, no giving way, no difficulty with stairs or normal walking.
  - No calf tenderness or signs of deep venous thrombosis reported.
  - Alert and oriented during consultation.

Impression:
- Right knee mechanical/overuse pain temporally associated with recent increase in running distance; clicking present. One transient episode of right toe tingling. Further clinical assessment required to exclude internal derangement.

Management Plan:
- Conservative management advised:
  - Continue ice therapy as already used.
  - Reduce running/intensity; avoid running through pain; modify marathon training until symptoms improve.
  - Oral NSAIDs acceptable; clinician offered a stronger anti-inflammatory prescription to replace over-the-counter ibuprofen (prescription to be sent to pharmacy). (Prescribed agent name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.)
  - Avoid concurrent use of prescribed anti-inflammatory with ibuprofen.
- Referrals and investigations:
  - Referral to physiotherapy arranged for clinical assessment and initial management.
  - Consider imaging (e.g., to assess cartilage/ligaments) if recommended after physiotherapy assessment.
- Safety-netting / urgent signs:
  - Return for urgent medical review if persistent swelling, increased heat/redness of knee, systemic symptoms (fever/feeling unwell), or if knee locks and you cannot bend/straighten it.

Patient Summary:
- Patient Mary Jo developed right knee pain with clicking over ~2 weeks after increasing long runs while training for a marathon. Ice relieves symptoms; currently full range of motion with no ongoing swelling. Plan is conservative management with ice, reduced running, physiotherapy referral, and a prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory sent to the pharmacy; urgent review advised for worsening signs.

Key Takeaways:
- Use ice regularly and reduce running intensity; do not run through pain.
- A stronger prescribed anti-inflammatory will be sent to your pharmacy; do not combine with over-the-counter ibuprofen.
- Attend physiotherapy for assessment and targeted treatment; seek urgent care for increased swelling, redness, fever, or inability to move the knee.

Next Steps:
- Physiotherapy appointment for formal examination and rehabilitation plan (referral to be sent).
- Prescription for a stronger anti-inflammatory to be sent to the pharmacy (drug name/dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript).
- Possible clinic review or imaging if symptoms persist or if physiotherapist recommends further investigation.
- Return/phone contact if urgent symptoms develop as listed above.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No documented allergies.
  - No clinician-measured vital signs.
  - No documented objective knee examination findings (inspection, palpation, ligament tests, joint line tenderness, effusion quantification).
  - Specific name/dose/route/frequency of the prescribed stronger anti-inflammatory not documented.
  - No formal documentation of pharmacy name/dispensing confirmation.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Initial statement suggested "knees" hurting/clicking, but later clarified symptoms are primarily the right knee — conflict noted.
  - Patient uncertain about Aleve drug class and equated it with acetaminophen — medication classification conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally clear; occasional filler words and minor conversational interruptions but clinically relevant information was discernible.
